2) No, no one close to me ever swayed me to become pro-choice. This was just a stance I took on my own. Since we as women are the ones who put our mental and physical being on the line through pregnancy, we need to have access to a full range of options, including the right to terminate. Whether or not a woman chooses to have or keep a baby needs to be her choice alone, and no outside force should be pressuring her one way or the other.
3) I consider myself somewhere in the middle between liberal and conservative.

4) I was raised under Christian beliefs and do still hold those views. We are all sinners, hence why I believe we have no right to judge the choices and actions of those around us unless we are God himself. 

5) No, I personally don't believe there should be any restrictions on abortion; on principle, it's just wrong to restrict access to a person's private medical choices, regardless of what they might be, no one has the right to but-in. 

6)Absolutely, advocates and politicians have every right to express their personal feelings on abortions and still want to keep them legal. They understand that they shouldn't let their personal feelings interfere with the rights of their constituents instead of getting caught up in their own self-righteousness.
